passage: Architect Zaha Hadid ______ designed buildings whose sweeping, fluid geometries seemed to defy conventional construction, from the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku to the London Aquatics Centre built for the 2012 Olympic Games.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize,
, the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize
the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize
, the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize,

explanation:
**Choice D is correct.** The blank holds a nonrestrictive appositive, which Standard English sets off with a matched pair of commas: ", the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize,".

**The Full Solution:**
- The phrase is supplementary — "Architect Zaha Hadid" already identifies her uniquely, so the appositive could be removed without changing who is meant.
- A nonrestrictive appositive takes paired bracketing marks; with no internal commas in the phrase, paired commas are the conventional choice, letting the main clause read through unbroken.

**Why the other choices are wrong:**
- A: It supplies only the closing comma, leaving the appositive fused to the name on its left.
- B: It supplies only the opening comma, so the appositive crashes into the verb "designed" with no closing boundary.
- C: It omits both commas, treating the supplementary phrase as if it restricted which Zaha Hadid is meant.

_meta.rule: paired commas around a nonrestrictive appositive (no internal commas)
_meta.anchor: Zaha Hadid — first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize (2004); Heydar Aliyev Center; London Aquatics Centre

distractors.A: closing comma only (appositive fused to the name on the left)
distractors.B: opening comma only (surface-match to the start of the paired pattern, missing close)
distractors.C: no commas (treats the appositive as restrictive)
